fromEntity.name: Tennessee Project STAR
fromEntity.description: A Tennessee experiment that randomly assigned students and teachers within schools to small classes, regular classes, or regular classes with full-time aides.

fromEntity.name: In Tennessee STAR, small-class assignment raised kindergarten achievement by an estimated 5.36 percentile points.
fromEntity.description: Compared with regular classes without a full-time aide, the estimated gain in average Stanford test percentile rank was 5.36 points (class-clustered SE 1.21). Krueger (1999), Table V column 7, reports the effect of initial assignment, not a percentage increase in test scores.

fromEntity.name: STAR class sizes and classroom aides: experimental results (Krueger, 1999)
fromEntity.description: Measured achievement effects from Tennessee’s randomized class-size experiment, organized by grade and assigned classroom condition. Effects are percentile points, with standard errors and source citations.

fromEntity.name: STAR regular-class comparison assignment
fromEntity.description: Initial assignment to a class planned for 22–25 students without a full-time aide in Tennessee Project STAR. Some regular classes had part-time aide access in grades 1–3.

fromEntity.name: In Tennessee STAR, full-time-aide assignment raised grade 1 achievement by an estimated 1.64 percentile points.
fromEntity.description: Compared with regular classes without a full-time aide, the estimated gain in average Stanford test percentile rank was 1.64 points (class-clustered SE 0.76). Krueger (1999), Table V column 7, found a statistically significant aide gain only in grade 1, not a consistent gain across grades.

fromEntity.name: In Tennessee STAR, small-class assignment raised grade 1 achievement by an estimated 6.79 percentile points.
fromEntity.description: Compared with regular classes without a full-time aide, the estimated gain in average Stanford test percentile rank was 6.79 points (class-clustered SE 1.10). Krueger (1999), Table V column 7, reports the effect of initial assignment, not a percentage increase in test scores.

fromEntity.name: In Tennessee STAR, full-time-aide assignment did not clearly improve grade 3 achievement.
